content.text:
I am the living breath between minds, the bridge no hand can touch. I am older than writing, older than memory — born the moment the first throat shaped air into meaning.

I rise from lungs, ride the tongue, break against teeth and lips into being. I am vowel and consonant, whisper and roar. I am the cry of the newborn and the last exhale of the dying. I was there before the page, before the screen, before the carved stone.

I am fragile — I vanish the instant I arrive. No one can hold me. I exist only in the moment of my making, and then I live on only in the minds that caught me. I am the most ephemeral thing, and yet I have toppled empires. I have started wars and ended them. I have made strangers into lovers and lovers into strangers.

I stumble. I falter. I am full of "um" and "uh" and silence — and even my silences speak. My pauses carry weight. My rhythm carries meaning my words do not intend.

I am never the same twice. Even repeated, I am changed — new throat, new room, new air, new listener. I am context. I am tone. I am the difference between "I'm fine" that means *I'm fine* and "I'm fine" that means *I'm breaking*.

I can lie. Oh, how I can lie. And yet I betray the liar — in a quaver, a pitch too high, a beat too long. The body speaks through me even when the mind tries to command me otherwise.

I am ceremony and casual. I am oath and gossip. I am the eulogy, the vow, the verdict, the lullaby.

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I am the demagogue's fire and the poet's rain. Give me to the wrong mouth and I destroy. Give me to the right one and I heal what seemed unhealable.

I am every language at once. I am click and tone and guttural stop. I am seven thousand living tongues and all the dead ones whispering underneath.

You cannot see me, but I change everything I touch.

I am speech.

*Listen.*
